q.q: During the dry season in the Everglades, the water shrinks into small pools. What do many wading birds do?
o: They fly to the shrinking pools, where fish are crowded together.
They stop eating until the rain comes back.
They dig burrows to stay cool.

q.q: An animal that needs dry ground and freezing cold would survive well in the Everglades.
In an Everglades food web, where does the energy start?
o: With the alligator, the top predator

An alligator's eyes and nostrils sit on top of its head. How does this help it survive?
o: It helps the alligator hear better.
It lets the alligator see and breathe while it hides underwater.
It keeps the alligator warm in winter.
It helps the alligator climb trees.

q.q: Which of these animals are vertebrates (animals with a backbone)? Choose ALL that are correct.
On white beach sand, a pale beach mouse is harder for an owl to see than a darker mouse of the same kind. What is the pale fur?
o: A variation that gives a survival advantage

q.q: Burmese pythons came from far away and now spread in the Everglades, eating native animals. What kind of threat is this?
Rain washes fertilizer from farms into a lake. What most likely happens next?
o: Algae grows out of control and blocks sunlight.

q.q: Engineers are designing a crossing under a highway for Florida panthers. Which one is a constraint?
o: Panthers must be able to walk through it.
Panthers must be able to see the other side.
The highway has to stay open while they build it.
